spec.name: Strandbeest Wind Walker
spec.description: A Theo Jansen-style kinetic sculpture: a yellow PVC-tube beach creature on eight Holy-Number linkage legs, with crank axles, bottle lungs on its back, and cream wind sails on a mast.
spec.layout:
Everything is yellow PVC tube with dark elbow connectors, white zip ties, steel axles and cream sailcloth, like a beach sculpture built from pipe. +Z is the front; the creature walks toward it. From front to back: (1) a tapering tube prow or nose at z 1.9..2.6 with two bottle 'eyes' and a small wind vane. (2) Behind it the body: two long frame rails with zig-zag triangle bracing, at y about 1.0..1.4 and |x| about 0.38. (3) Four leg stations per side on that frame. (4) A bottle-lung rack (blue and green flat bottles with orange caps and little piston rods) along the top of the frame, y 1.4..1.8. (5) At the back, a mast at z about -1.4 rising to y about 2.5, carrying two big cream triangular sails that fan out to either side (|x| up to 1.0), with yellow battens, rope rigging and a bright pennant on top. Only the feet touch the floor.

LEG TEMPLATE (shared by all 8 legs, built in a plane). Each leg is a Jansen-style linkage of 2D nodes (u forward = +Z, v up = +Y, in meters, measured from its hip pivot P):
P(0,0) frame pivot; C(-0.30,-0.08) crank axle centre; K(-0.30,-0.26) crank pin, which hangs straight down from C at rest; A(-0.42,0.22); B(-0.80,-0.14); D(-0.46,-0.50); E(-0.10,-0.46); F(0.05,-1.11) foot.
Links (each a rod about 0.022 m radius, yellow): C-K (crank arm), P-A, K-A, A-B, K-B, B-D, P-E, E-D, D-F, E-F.
Nodes get dark connector spheres or elbows of radius 0.03, F gets a rubber ball foot of radius 0.05 with an orange cap, and a few white zip ties sit across the joints.
Model position of a node = (x = side * planeX, y = 1.15 + v, z = hipZ + u). Make each link a double rod, one at planeX - 0.03 and one at planeX + 0.03, joined by short spacer bolts at the nodes, so the legs read as thick sculpture. The foot centre is at y about 0.04, so the foot sinks about 0.01 m into the floor. All eight legs use the same rest pose.
Leg stations (hipZ, planeX magnitude): 1: (1.5, 0.62); 2: (0.5, 0.85); 3: (-0.5, 0.62); 4: (-1.5, 0.85). Left side is +X and right is -X; build both sides. Each crank axle runs along X at y 1.07, z = hipZ - 0.30, so it passes exactly through node C of both left and right legs. Each frame pivot axle runs along X at y 1.15, z = hipZ, through node P.

parts.builds: The chassis and the face. Two long yellow PVC side rails at x = ±0.38, y 1.22, from z -2.0 to 1.95. A lower keel tube at y 1.0 along x = 0. Vertical posts and a zig-zag of triangle bracing between the rails and keel (triangulated like a Jansen frame), dark elbow connectors at every junction, and white zip ties. Cross tubes at each pivotAxle station that carry the axle bearings (steel-dark pillow blocks where the axles pass through). At the front, a tapering tube prow runs from noseRoot to noseTip: a slim swept beak made of two converging tubes with a cross brace. Two big bottle 'eyes' (short cylinders with a dome, eyeWhite with rubber pupil discs and a teal ring) sit on either side of the nose root, facing forward, and a small brass wind-vane spinner (a cross of thin rods with a rubber tip) rises above the nose. Colours: pvcYellow for tubes, pvcYellowDark on the underside and keel, elbowInk connectors, zipWhite ties, steelDark bearings. No bottle rack, axles, legs or sail here.
parts.attaches: Rails carry the bearing blocks that the driveline's pivotAxle1..4 and crankAxle1..4 pass through; the rack stands on frameRailL/R at rackTop; the mast foot sits on the rails at mastBase. The face rides head and the frame rides body.

parts.builds: Four Jansen linkage legs, from stations 1 and 2 on both sides (legL1, legR1 at hipZ 1.5 with planeX 0.62; legL2, legR2 at hipZ 0.5 with planeX 0.85). Each leg is built from the LEG TEMPLATE in the layout: ten double yellow PVC link rods joined at the nodes P, C, K, A, B, D, E and F, with elbowInk connector spheres, spacer bolts, white zip ties at the joints, steelDark pin heads, and a pvcYellowDark band where the long links cross. At each foot there is a rubber ball foot with a capOrange cap and a small brass ankle collar. The pin node K gets a brass bushing. Do not build the axles, the crank arms or the discs on the axles, since the driveline owns them, but each leg's C and P node connector must sit on the axle line. The legs are the only parts that touch the floor.
parts.attaches: Hip nodes P at hipL1/R1 and hipL2/R2 sit on the pivot axles pivotAxle1 and pivotAxle2; node C sits on crankAxle1 and crankAxle2, and node K is the crank pin on the end of the driveline's crank arm.

parts.builds: Four Jansen linkage legs, from stations 3 and 4 on both sides (legL3, legR3 at hipZ -0.5 with planeX 0.62; legL4, legR4 at hipZ -1.5 with planeX 0.85), built identically to the LEG TEMPLATE in the layout: double yellow PVC link rods, elbowInk node connectors, spacer bolts, zip ties, steelDark pins, brass bushing on node K, rubber ball feet with capOrange caps. Add a driftwood-brown (use rope colour) wrapped grip band at the top of each leg's P-A rod as a sculpture detail. Do not build the axles, the crank arms or the discs on the axles.
parts.attaches: Hip nodes P at hipL3/R3 and hipL4/R4 sit on pivotAxle3 and pivotAxle4; node C sits on crankAxle3 and crankAxle4; node K is the crank pin on the end of the driveline's crank arm.

parts.builds: The mechanism and the lungs. (1) Four pivot axles (steel rods along X at pivotAxle1..4, running from x = -0.95 to 0.95, riding body) and four crank axles (along X at crankAxle1..4, same span, one per crank joint), with brass collars and end caps on the axle ends outside the legs, and steelDark nuts. (2) On each crank axle, at the planeX of each leg on both sides, a crank arm: a short brass bar 0.18 m long from the axle centre straight down to the crank pin K (crank axle y 1.07, pin at y 0.89, same z), with a pin cylinder pointing out along X, and a small brass disc at the axle hub. Add a few toothed cog discs (steel, 12 teeth) on the crank axles between the frame rails. (3) The bottle-lung rack on the back: two rows of 5 flat plastic bottles per side (bottleBlue and bottleGreen cylinders with tapered necks and capOrange caps, lying along Z on the rails between y 1.4 and 1.75), held by pvcYellow cradles and zip ties, with thin steel piston rods and tiny tube hoses (teal) running from the caps down toward the crank axles. Everything on the axles rides the crank joints; the rack and pivot axles ride body.
parts.attaches: The axles pass through the frame's bearing blocks at the pivotAxle and crankAxle mounts and through the leg nodes P and C. The crank pin heads at K meet the legs. The bottle rack sits on frameRailL/R at rackTop and stays clear of the mast base at z -1.4 (the rack ends at z -1.0).

parts.builds: The wind sails at the back. A yellow PVC mast at mastBase rising and leaning slightly back to mastTop (y 2.45), with a base block, dark elbow collars and zip ties. Two big triangular cream sails (thin extruded or membrane panels in sailCream, with shaded sailShade bands near the root and stitched seam strips) fan out left and right from the mast, each hung on a yellow leading spar that runs from the mast top out and down to a wing tip at about (±0.98, 1.75, -1.2), with a trailing spar to (±0.95, 1.65, -2.6). Add 4 yellow batten tubes across each sail, a small jib sail forward of the mast, brass grommets along the edges, and rope-coloured rigging lines from the mast top to the spar tips and to the frame. A bright pennantRed streamer flag flies from the mast top on a short spar, with a brass finial. At each sail tip hangs a small bottleBlue float with a capOrange cap. A rear arch of two tubes behind the mast at z -2.6 supports the sail trailing edges. The sail stays above the legs and the rack.
parts.attaches: The mast foot sits on the frame rails at mastBase and its foot block rides the mast joint, which is parented to body. Rigging lines end at frameRailL/R near z -1.9 and z -0.8.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching a Strandbeest-style wind-walking sculpture, aiming for roughly 2.6 wide, 2.2 tall, and 4.0 long, and I'm listing the parts it needs, starting with the yellow tubes, the sails at the back, and the leg linkages.

I'm laying out the creature's body in regions so each part can be built on its own: a central truss spine with crank shafts and cross-bracing, the front head with bottle sensors, and the cams. The legs will go in separate banks on each side, with each leg module a Jansen linkage given its own phase offset.

I'm working out how to split the creature into regions, with front and rear leg banks on each side and a sail structure at the back, rising to about 2.2 meters. I'm also thinking about whether the skeleton should have joints at all, since a kinetic sculpture might need a root body and crank hinges along the x axis.

I'm working out the leg layout now: three leg modules per side, spaced along the length at roughly 1.3 meters apart, with each leg's crank offset by 120 degrees from its neighbor.

I'm working out the leg placement now: the leg planes sit at about x = ±0.6 for the front and rear modules and near ±0.8 for the middle one, so the linkages don't collide where they overlap along the length.

I'm settling the leg planes at different x offsets, roughly 0.55, 0.8, and 1.05 from the center, so the three leg modules per side don't collide along the length. I'm also sketching the leg geometry in a local frame around a hip pivot near one meter up, with the crank radius scaled to match the overall height.

I'm working out the leg linkage numbers now, using the Jansen proportions with a scale of about 0.01 to 0.0125 meters per unit, so the leg spans roughly 1.2 meters. I'm also setting the frame pivot at about 1.3 meters up and the foot near ground level, leaving the leg builders to compute the crank center from there.

I'm working out the linkage coordinates for one leg, planning to give builders explicit joint points instead of asking them to solve the Holy Numbers themselves. I'm checking the crank center and frame pivot placement against the standard Jansen geometry, measured from a fixed origin.

I'm recalling the standard Jansen linkage proportions, with the crank center at (38, 7.8) and a crank pin at radius 15 from it. The next joints depend on distances like b = 41.5 from the pin and j = 50 from the pivot, and I'd rather pin those down from the reference values than compute each position by hand.

I'm now picking approximate hand-chosen coordinates for a Jansen-style leg rather than exact values, since the exact linkage numbers aren't needed for an abstract sculpture. I'll define the leg geometry in a local 2D frame with the hip pivot at the origin.

I'm estimating the leg's joint positions in meters, with the crank center sitting just behind and below the hip pivot. The scale is still open: at 0.01 m per unit the leg looks too short, so I'm trying about 0.012 m per unit to reach the foot near the floor.

I'm picking a scale of about 0.0125 meters per unit, with the pivot about 1.15 meters off the floor. I'm placing the crank center behind the pivot and working out where the crank pin sits below it.

I'm now working out the leg's joint positions by intersecting circles: one linkage at distance 41.5 from the pivot and another at 50 from the crank pin, which gives the upper joint's location.

I'm working out approximate joint positions for a Jansen-style leg, starting from the pivot and the crank pin, and checking the distances to the upper joint against the link lengths. I'm dropping exact Holy Numbers in favor of a hand-built template with roughly consistent lengths, since that's enough for an abstract sculpture.

I'm placing the leg's pivot, crank center, and crank pin in meters relative to the hip, and I'm starting to sketch the linkage rods that connect them to the upper joints.

I'm trying to place the leg's pivot, crank center, and crank pin in a local frame, and I'm picking rough coordinates for the rods that link them, without worrying about exact Jansen values.

I'm assigning rough coordinates to the leg's pivot, crank pin, and upper joints, checking that the rods P–A and K–A come out near half a meter long. The lower joints are still giving the linkage a shape I'm not yet settled on.

I'm laying out the leg's node positions relative to the hip pivot, with a chain of triangles resembling a Jansen linkage rather than exact values. I'm placing the crank center, crank pin, and upper joints roughly, then sketching the lower joints and foot to finish the leg's outline.

I'm settling the leg's node table: the hip pivot at the origin, the crank axle and pin just behind it, and the upper and lower joints placed to form a Jansen-like chain. The foot node sits slightly forward of the pivot, low enough to reach the floor.

I'm listing the leg's link connections now: the crank rod, the upper and lower bars, and the shin triangle that reaches down to the foot. I'm checking the lengths of the foot-side links, which come out roughly right even if not exact.

I'm settling the body frame around that same hip height, placing the crank axle just below the pivot and running across the width of the sculpture. I'm sketching the central truss at roughly 1.0 to 1.5 meters up, with a pivot rod along the x axis at the hip position.

I'm now spacing the leg stations along the length at four positions, z = 1.5, 0.5, -0.5 and -1.5, so each leg gets its own room and the linkages stay clear of each other.

I'm settling the leg planes at two inner-and-outer offsets, about 0.62 and 0.82 from the centerline, so adjacent stations stay clear of each other. I'm weighing whether to double each leg with a second, phase-shifted plane, but I'll leave that out for now to keep the part count manageable.

I'm settling the leg planes at different offsets: the inner pair at about 0.60 from the centerline and the outer pair at 0.85, alternating across the stations. I'm keeping every leg on the same rest-pose template with the crank pin straight down, rather than varying the crank phase per leg, since that would change the linkage shape.

I'm settling the foot height so the foot sits just above the floor, then checking the overall size: about 2.4 meters tall with the sails, roughly 5.2 meters long from the sails at the back to the nose, and the legs reaching out to about 0.85 meters from the centerline.

I'm laying out the frame as a truss: two side rails at about x = ±0.38 running most of the length, a lower keel rail down the centre, and cross-frames at each leg station with zigzag bracing. The hub for the axles and the yellow tube "muscles" will sit along that truss.

I'm listing the frame's finishing touches: a row of translucent blue bottles along the top, a tapering prow at the nose with a wind-vane and two bottle-cap eyes. I'm also noting the leg stations, with front legs at the first two positions and rear legs at the last two, plus the crank axles and discs that will drive them.

I'm settling the parts list for the sculpture into five groups: the frame and nose, the front and rear leg banks, a driveline with the pivot and crank axles and pump bottles along the top, and the sail rig at the back.

I'm settling the sail rig now: a mast near the rear rising toward 2.5 meters, with spars fanning out to support two large cream sail panels, a small jib, and a bottle-based wind-vane on top. I'm also considering whether the body needs a root joint at the centre with crank hinges along the x axis.

I'm listing the joint definitions for the rig: four crank axles along the x axis at the body, eight leg joints hanging from the hip pivot, plus the body root and the sail's mast base.

I'm now sorting out the leg planes and crank axles: the left legs sit at x = +0.62 and +0.85 on alternating stations, the right legs mirror them, and each crank axle sits just ahead of its leg station.

I'm checking the spacing around the leg stations: the front hip sits about a third of a meter ahead of its crank axle, so the two shouldn't interfere. The front leg's rear joint reaches back toward the next station, but the offset in x keeps the linkages clear of each other.

I'm checking the leg planes against the frame rails and the crank axles, confirming that the crank axle passes cleanly through the leg plane at its pivot node. The outer leg planes sit clear of the rails, and the axles extend out past them with collars.

I'm listing the palette next, a set of named colours for the yellow tubing, sail cream, bottle blues and greens, steel axles, and ink, staying under two dozen entries.

Now I'm sketching the bounding boxes for the front legs and the frame, roughly fitting each part's space into the overall budget.

I'm checking the legs' footprints in z against the next station, since the front leg's foot reaches about 1.62 and the rear station's forward reach is only a short way ahead of the front station's back joint, so the overlap is only in z and the x planes keep them apart.

I'm setting the bounding boxes for the driveline, which holds the axles, crank arms, cogs, collars, and the bottle pump rack, with a height band of roughly 0.8 to 1.8. It will overlap the frame box a little, but the parts interleave, so that's acceptable.

I'm now setting the sail rig's footprint, with the mast near z = -1.4 and its span running from about y = 1.4 up to 2.5. The overall length comes out to roughly 5.3 meters, with the sails spanning about the width of the axles.

I'm settling the sail rig: two triangular cream sail panels with yellow battens, rigged from a mast near the back, with a red-orange pennant on top and blue bottle floats at the tips. I'm also adding a head joint at the nose and a sail joint at the mast base, with the mast running upward from z = -1.4.

I'm assigning the leg joints legL1 through legL4 and their right-side mirrors at the hip positions, each with the body as parent and the leg role. I'm also placing the four crank joints at y 1.07 along the body, then splitting the parts so the driveline rides the cranks and the frame rides the body.

I'm defining the leg mapping and tube sizes, then settling on a double-plane layout with spacer bolts. Next I'm writing the palette as JSON and drafting the leg template table along with the style rules.

I'm writing up the style rules for the leg tubes: yellow PVC pipe with dark elbow connectors and white zip ties, and then I'll set the palette and layout down in the final file.
